gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-tagbanwa: Round, open curves with clear gaps and lowercase that fills most of its height give Noto Sans Tagbanwa a friendly, easy look. Quilon above it is the opposite, a display face with a thin-to-thick stroke so slight that its commanding tone stays gentle.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-tai-le: Quilon draws its strokes with a gentle swell and thin, so the large openings inside its tall letters feel editorial without shouting. Noto Sans Tai Le follows with strokes that taper out before touching, and its small capital step keeps the text quiet.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-tangsa: Quilon's big open counters and slow shift in stroke thickness give its headings a commanding, editorial presence. And Noto Sans Tangsa settles into text with wide round openings and short ascender stems, so a long page would read smoothly.
